chunks: 906 - Bilal used to call the adhan after the morning, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, Ibn Umm Maktum calls the adhan during the night,
so when you hear his adhan, then eat and drink until you hear the adhan of Bilal.”

key_terms.أَذَانَهُ: his adhan, referring to the call of Ibn Umm Maktum
key_terms.ابْنَ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ: Ibn Umm Maktum, who used to give the adhan during the night
key_terms.الصُّبْحِ: the morning, referring here to the time of Fajr
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: during the night, before the true dawn
key_terms.بِلالٌ: Bilal, the mu'adhdhin whose adhan marked the relevant morning time
key_terms.فَكُلُوا: then eat, indicating permissibility before the final cutoff
key_terms.وَاشْرَبُوا: and drink, indicating permissibility before the adhan of Bilal
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنُ: calls the adhan, announces the prayer time

ai.seo_question: When should one stop eating and drinking before the Fajr fast begins?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the distinction between an adhan given before the true break of dawn and the adhan marking the actual onset of Fajr. It indicates that eating and drinking remain permitted until the adhan of Bilal, which signaled the beginning of the morning time relevant to fasting.
